Additional detail from a `--log-level DEBUG` run (ruling out the common 'add enabled:true / OAuth' advice):

- Config already has `"enabled": true`; the server logs no config error, no OAuth URL, and no process-startup failure. The MCP server connects (`GET /mcp` -> `connected`).
- For an API-driven session, the DEBUG log shows a per-request `creating instance` for the project directory, cleanly bootstrapping (loading config -> watcher -> booting location services), with MCP initialized lazily afterward - but the resulting turn still exposes zero MCP tools to the model.
- By contrast, a TUI run against the identical config logs an `evaluated permission=pingtest_ping_test ... action=allow` line (the model actually invoking the tool). The API run logs no tool at all.

So this isn't a config/enabled/OAuth issue - it's specifically that the per-request instance used for an API session doesn't surface the connected MCP server's tools, whereas the persistent TUI instance does.

I can confirm this on OpenCode 1.18.4 on Linux with a second process writing to the same PTY. This is not limited to plugin or MCP output.

In our reproducible case, a wrapper started a local HTTP server and then launched OpenCode in the foreground. The server inherited the wrapper's `stdout`/`stderr`. When OpenCode made a model request, the sibling server printed a request trace (including JSON) to `stderr`; those bytes were painted over the active OpenCode TUI. Resizing the terminal immediately restored the correct frame. Screenshots of the corrupted frame and resize repaint are in [link-assistant/formal-ai#819](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/819#issuecomment-5055516309).

The core process shape was:

```sh
(while sleep 2; do printf '[background] diagnostic\n' >&2; done) &
opencode .
```

Our application-level fix is to redirect the background server's `stdout` and `stderr` to a durable log before launching OpenCode. A PTY regression now verifies that a unique request-body marker never reaches the terminal stream. That fully prevents the corruption in our wrapper, but OpenCode still appears vulnerable to any unrelated process that retains the same terminal descriptors.

Expected defensive behavior: if external terminal output arrives while the fullscreen renderer owns the terminal, perform a complete redraw (or otherwise restore cursor/frame state) so the bytes cannot remain inside the input/status region.

I think a rejected `fs/write_text_file` can currently turn into a false successful edit.

`drainPendingWrites()` removes the item and records `flushedContent` before the RPC runs. `flushPendingWrites()` then catches a rejection and resolves, while the event path has already sent the completed tool update. The end-of-turn `enqueueUnflushed()` skips the content as already flushed, and `clear()` drops the remaining overlay entry. In a focused fixture with a rejecting `writeTextFile`, I get one RPC call, an empty pending queue, no end-of-turn retry, and the real file is still unchanged.

Would it make sense to acknowledge/remove each item only after the RPC succeeds, and make rejection fail the tool/turn, with a regression test for a rejecting client?
